claims.statement: EU battery law requires qualifying EV batteries to expose current state-of-health data in the BMS to lawful purchasers or their agents for residual-value and reuse assessment.

Battery passports become mandatory from 18 February 2027 for relevant newly placed EV batteries and include performance, durability, reuse, and recycling information, so they do not solve near-term coverage of the legacy fleet.
Independent certificate supply is already mature: AVILOO and DEKRA offer rapid model-specific tests, and BCA embeds AVILOO reports in European BEV auctions for EUR 40 per tested vehicle.

The Commission still describes automotive data access as fragmented and potentially needing complementary measures beyond the Data Act, so legal entitlement is not equivalent to a uniform technical interface.

A Poland-first entrant could pilot through licensed diagnostics and dealer partners, but a defensible exchange requires local resale outcomes and transaction integration rather than another standalone certificate.

contrary_evidence: BCA already combines an independent battery report with a large European auction and charges only EUR 40 per report.
AVILOO advertises a EUR 99 retail certificate, below the original 700 PLN certificate hypothesis.
DEKRA and AVILOO have model-specific algorithms and accumulated test databases that a new entrant would initially lack.
Battery-passport and BMS-access rights do not create a uniform interface for the existing used-EV fleet.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot with two to five Warsaw and Wielkopolska fleet lessors or high-volume used-EV dealers by processing an actual disposal batch, using licensed incumbent test outputs and capturing bids and realized outcomes only with participant permission. Do not launch a general exchange until repeated paid batches and lawful outcome access demonstrate a recurring workflow.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The prior path dependent on roughly 15000 annual one-off certificates is replaced by a still-unvalidated recurring fleet-account path: prove paid repeat batches, positive annual contribution per account, and a compounding outcome dataset before projecting any route or timing to 5 million PLN of founder net worth. Current evidence supports no conservative valuation or timing claim.
economics.founder_time: About 15-20 hours weekly if licensed partners perform physical tests and vehicle handling while the founder builds data normalization, bid and sale-outcome workflows, integrations, and bounded account management.
economics.gross_margin_basis: No diagnostic resale margin is assumed. Contribution must be measured after licensed-test, integration, support, liability, failed-test, and transaction-handling costs against any recurring workflow or completed-sale fee.
economics.payback: The earlier 850-certificate payback claim is withdrawn. Payback cannot be estimated until paid batches establish pricing, test and integration cost, vehicles processed per account, repeat cadence, and contribution after failures and support.
economics.pricing: Validate a per-batch or recurring remarketing-workflow fee, with a transaction fee only when the service actually sources a buyer and a sale closes; no fee level or willingness to pay is assumed.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Fleet lessors and high-volume dealers can have recurring disposal batches, unlike a one-off certificate per vehicle, but repeat cadence, outcome-data access, and account retention remain unvalidated.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A diagnostic-agnostic Polish dataset linking normalized incumbent test outputs and vehicle attributes to bids, realized sale prices, buyer route, and time-to-sale
fingerprint.customer: Polish fleet lessors and high-volume used-EV dealers disposing of recurring vehicle batches
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Direct fleet-disposal batch pilots and remarketing-workflow integrations, followed by account expansion only after repeat paid batches
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Battery-informed fleet remarketing workflow and residual-value intelligence using licensed incumbent diagnostics, monetized through recurring or per-batch workflow fees and completed-sale fees rather than a proprietary certificate
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Fleet owner or dealer pays when a disposal batch is processed; an additional transaction fee applies only when the service sources the buyer and the sale closes, with all fee levels unvalidated
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A fleet or dealer must dispose of a used-EV batch without Polish outcome evidence for reserve prices, buyer routing, or the resale effect of battery condition

founder_fit: Normalizing diagnostics and modeling residual value fit the founder's data-science and renewable-energy background.
Licensed partners can keep physical testing and vehicle handling bounded while the founder focuses on software and analytics.
The narrowed fleet-account model still requires deliberate B2B selling and data permissions, but not a public personal brand.

redesign.economic_effect: This abandons the price-compressed one-off certificate path and makes licensed incumbent tests an input to a recurring fleet-disposal workflow, so the conservative economic unit becomes annual contribution per repeat account and completed batch rather than 15000 certificates. It does not establish paid batches, pricing, contribution, outcome-data rights, retention, or a 5 million PLN founder-net-worth path.

risks: Incorrect or overstated certificates can create valuation, warranty, and safety liability.
AVILOO, DEKRA, BCA, OEM programs, or another auction can compress price and capture the transaction data.
Unsupported models, inconclusive tests, and proprietary interfaces can interrupt service coverage.
A certificate may improve trust without producing enough incremental sale value to support acquisition cost.
Fleet owners or auction partners may withhold closed-sale outcomes, preventing the proposed data loop from compounding.
BCA, AVILOO, DEKRA, OEM programs, or fleet software vendors can add equivalent local remarketing analytics through their existing distribution.

structure.commercial_archetype: B2B fleet remarketing workflow and residual-value data service
structure.control_point: Permissioned closed-loop linkage of licensed diagnostics to bids, routing decisions, realized sale prices, and time-to-sale
structure.critical_dependency: Repeat paid fleet batches, lawful access to closed transaction outcomes, and enough decision improvement to justify a workflow fee despite incumbent auctions

thesis: Provide a diagnostic-agnostic batch remarketing workflow for Polish fleet lessors and high-volume used-EV dealers, using licensed incumbent battery tests as inputs and binding them to bids, realized sale prices, and time-to-sale so the business competes on local disposal decisions and outcome data rather than on another battery certificate.
title: Polish EV Remarketing Intelligence
uncertainties: Polish dealers' willingness to pay above embedded European auction pricing is untested.
No evidence yet shows insurers, lenders, or buyers will accept a new certificate methodology.
Supported-model coverage, license cost, test failure rate, and professional-indemnity cost are unknown.
The incremental sale-price or conversion lift in Poland has not been independently measured.
No evidence yet establishes paid repeat disposal batches, lawful permission to retain closed-sale outcomes, or measurable improvement in reserve prices, routing, conversion, or time-to-sale.
No exclusive diagnostic, fleet, dealer, auction, buyer, insurer, or lender commitment is established by this redesign.
